messages:
Marta: quick design check — dropping a staging screenshot of the new Quiet window panel. Thinking about how the quiet window ties into channel mapping + escalation. https://imgur.com/preview-quiet-window :eyes:
Andre: first pass: I like the compact row for channels but worried "Quiet window" language might be confusing. Users often look for 'snooze' or 'mute'. Can we test alternate copy?
Kai: a11y note: make sure the timepickers are keyboard operable and the panel doesn't trap focus. Also need aria-live for the preview summary when users change times.
Anne: product question — in the preview, can we show who actually receives the alert during a quiet window (primary channel vs fallback/escalation)? Hard to reason about otherwise.
Samir: suggestion for channel mapping UI: show channel badges with a small chevron for priority. Allow drag-to-reorder; when a primary is suppressed, visually promote the next one and show a toast: "#team-oncall will be notified instead".
Marta: good — I'll mock the promoted badge state. Also thinking microcopy: primary vs fallback is subtle. Proposed copy: "Primary channel — first to be notified. Fallback channels — used if primary is unavailable or suppressed."
Andre: microcopy tweak: shorten to "Primary — first notified" and "Fallback — next in line". Keep it scannable.
Kai: color/contrast: the promoted badge uses green today — fails contrast at small sizes. Recommend darker outline + text instead of relying on background color alone.
Marta: noted. Also edge-case: what happens when a channel is removed while a quiet window is active? We should show an inline line: "Channel removed — alerts will follow escalation order." Otherwise users will be confused.
Anne: can we add a small "simulate" button in preview that shows a sample payload for integration owners? e.g., the webhook body with fields: channel, priority, suppressed: true/false. PMs love concrete examples.
Samir: +1 for simulate. Quick sketch of payload display:
```json
{
  "alert": "High error rate",
  "channel": "#team-oncall",
  "suppressed": true,
  "escalation": ["#backup-oncall"]
}
```
Marta: awesome — will include that as a collapsed disclosure under preview.
Andre: UI control nit: the quiet window toggle currently reads "Enable Quiet Window". For discoverability put the toggle left and label right so screenreaders read "Quiet window enabled" properly.
Kai: and add a visually-hidden label for the time inputs: aria-label="Quiet window start" / "Quiet window end". Also ensure the preview summary is a heading (h3) so assistive tech can jump there.
accessibility-bot: a11y checklist: 1) keyboard tab order validated, 2) labels + aria, 3) contrast >= 4.5:1 for small text, 4) live region for preview updates.
deploy-bot: deployed design mock to staging at https://staging.console.redwood/alerting/quiet-window (visual only).
Marta: follow-ups: I'll update the mock with copy changes, add simulate payload, and share an interactive Figma with keyboard flow. Will ping for a quick usability check tomorrow morning. :coffee:
